title: Literary passage plus a critic's reading
subtitle: Cross-Text Connections · 2 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **2 of the official questions in Cross-Text Connections are this one** — 0 Easy, 0 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- An italic intro says Text 1 is adapted from a novel or poem and Text 2 discusses that work, or Text 1 characterizes a work and Text 2 reappraises it.
- The question asks how the critic would interpret the excerpt, or how the critic would respond to a common view of the work.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Pull the critic's thesis from Text 2 in abstract terms, e.g. 'the work stages a tension between A and B' or 'it is more serious than its reputation'.
- 2) Find the image or feature in Text 1 that fits one side of that thesis.
- 3) Pick the choice that applies the critic's frame to that feature.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You answer from your own reading of the literary excerpt, which is often reasonable, instead of through Text 2's critical lens.
Choices that paraphrase Text 1's imagery vividly but ignore the critic's argument are the bait.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
